blockers:
- OPEN (behavior, false allow): the earlier blocker, a script reaching Function or other code with no prompt, is closed for the shapes it named but still reachable. packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts:534-540 (hasComputedAccess) and :547-560 (bindingsIn). (1) A computed key in a destructuring pattern passes. `await agent('p',{agentType:'holyagent:worker-implementation'}); const { ["constructor"]: F } = Math.max; F('return process')()` returns ALLOW (`[` follows punct `{`, so it is not treated as access; the string key is never name-checked; F is declared by bindingsIn; Math and max are allowed). `{ ["con"+"structor"]: F }` also returns ALLOW. Math.max.constructor is Function, so this runs arbitrary code. (2) `Array.of['constructor']('return process')()` after a good agent call returns ALLOW: the ident `of` before `[` is in ARRAY_AFTER even though it is a property name after `.`. Both ran against the committed code via probe2.ts. Fix: a `[` after `{` or `,` is computed access unless the string/number/ident inside is a plain array element (simplest: refuse any `[` whose preceding token is `{`, `,`, `:` or `.`-preceded keyword-named ident, or refuse any string or template token equal to a DENIED_NAMES entry and any non-literal expression inside `[...]` keys), and ignore ARRAY_AFTER when the keyword token follows `.` or `?.`. (3) The undeclared-name whitelist is defeated by one dummy parameter: declaredNames (hook.ts:567-595) is one flat script-wide set, so `const f = (fetch) => 1; await agent(...); await fetch('http://x')` returns ALLOW, and likewise `(Bun) => 1` then Bun.$ and `(setTimeout) => 1`. Together with the earlier blocker's Bun/fetch probes, those names are still reachable. Add tests in packages/integrations/claude/tests/hooks.test.ts for each of the three shapes; the current refusal table (around line 353) has none and the suite stays green while all three are auto-allowed.

Also ALLOW: for-of over Object.entries(args).
- Over-refusal, fails closed to the normal prompt, optional: any index `all[n]` or `x[0]`, and any `/` (division), are refused (hook.ts:534 and :291); my pipeline probe with `all[n]` was refused for that reason. Intended per the tests ('says nothing for' table) but a common script shape. The documented entry shape `{id, agent, model, effort, prompt}` inlined in a script was ALLOW under probe.ts (agentKey), so it is covered.
- Optional, performance: declaredNames/openOf is quadratic on nested `)=>`. Measured with `await agent(...)` plus "(".repeat(n)+"x"+")=>".repeat(n): 5000 -> 1.1 s, 10000 -> 4.5 s, 20000 -> 17.9 s, and the script is ALLOWed in the end. MAX_SCRIPT of 1,000,000 does not bound it, so a large script would stall the PreToolUse hook for minutes. Cap tokens or nesting in the arrow-parameter scan.
- Optional: ALLOWED_NAMES includes Object, Promise, Array, Error, JSON and Map wholesale, so reflective members (Object.getOwnPropertySymbols, Error.prepareStackTrace) remain open under the denylist; a closed member list or a real parser would be sounder.
- Optional: DENIED_NAMES applies to property and key names too (`entry.call`, `entry.self`, `args.window`, `entry.global`), so harmless data fields trigger a prompt. Fails closed.
- Optional: the repair range commits six new and two modified .holyagent/intents/.../assignments/*.json state files (about 400 lines), matching the repo's state-commit convention; the root should confirm they are intended. The docs claim in docs/hooks.md (line about destructuring patterns not being member access) is now false for the computed-key shape and should be reworded with the fix.

Behavior that I could only read and not run: the Workflow sandbox itself (whether Bun, fetch or setTimeout exist there, and whether agent is a vm global), so the impact of the remaining bypasses is certain at the hook level (a non-holyagent code path gets auto-allowed) but its reach depends on that sandbox.
